steps.note: Create the reverse auction in the eRFX flow.
Enable eRFX projects as required by the case.
A title is required to publish and to identify the event in the buyer list.
Configure the event as an auction.
Apply the auction pricing template before adding items.
Add the auction line item.
Complete the auction pricing sheet.
Commit a live bidding schedule.
Invite the QA vendor who will submit the bid.
Publish the reverse auction.
Confirm the event reached a published project page.
Confirm the vendor bid was accepted before attempting revocation.

args.need: in the vendor portal, open the live reverse auction, click Revoke on the bid of 100, and confirm the revocation

steps.note: No catalog step performs the vendor's Revoke action.
Return to the vendor portal to inspect the post-revocation vendor view.
Open this event's pricing round in the vendor portal.
Check for the vendor-side revoked status if the portal renders it.
Return to the buyer console while preserving the buyer session.
Reach the buyer's Events list as required by the scenario.
Confirm the list and its Live, History, Drafts, and Recurring navigation rendered.
Open the event created and bid on in this plan.
Open the buyer's Responses view.
Check whether the buyer-side response view displays a revoked marker.
Open the stage activity drawer to inspect the revocation record.
Check whether Order Activity records the bid revocation.
Open Master QCS as requested by the scenario; the step confirms the comparison grid rendered.
